topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, sets the context for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Biological Drivers of Cancer and Mutation
topics.groupedBecause: They define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous and inherited sources of mutation alongside microenvironmental factors.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: They examine environmental carcinogen exposures and use epidemiological data to evaluate how lifestyle and geography influence cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They explore how infectious pathogens drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the biochemical mechanisms by which physical agents and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation to damage DNA.

topics.label: Carcinogenic Initiation and Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: They distinguish between tumor initiators and promoters, showing how non-mutagenic agents stimulate cell proliferation through chronic inflammation and signaling pathways.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility and Mechanistic Summary
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how host developmental timing and tissue context modify cancer susceptibility, synthesizing the molecular mechanisms of carcinogenesis discussed.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: They outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Risk Assessment and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a summary of cancer causation and an overview of balancing environmental risks against practical benefits.
